# Sliding-Window Rate Limiter / Abuse IP Detection

## Problem

## Requirements

Rate-limiting variant:

- Signature: `rateLimit(userId: Identifier[], time: Integer[], k: Integer, t: Integer) -> Integer[]`.
- `userId` and `time` are parallel arrays; event `i` uses `userId[i]` and `time[i]`.
- Inputs are `userId[i]`, `time[i]`, `k`, and `t`.
- Return an integer array: use `1` when event `i` passes and `0` when it is rejected.
- A request may pass only when that user has fewer than `k` previously accepted requests with timestamps in the inclusive window `[time[i] - t, time[i]]`.
- Rejected requests must not affect later rate-limit checks.

Abusive-IP variant:

- Signature: `findAbusiveIPs(ip: IPAddress[], timestamp: Integer[], k: Integer, t: Integer) -> IPAddress[]`.
- Given parallel IP-address and timestamp arrays along with threshold `k` and duration `t`.
- Produce a unique array of all IP addresses occurring more than `k` times in at least one inclusive window of length `t`; the order is unspecified. Produce an empty array when no address meets that condition.

## Examples

```
ip = [4, 9, 4]
timestamp = [3, 7, 11]
k = 1
t = 10
Output: [4]
```

Address `4` occurs two times inside a 10-second interval.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

This is a sliding window count problem where you need to track the number of events per user within the last t time units.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a queue or a circular buffer per user to store timestamps of recent events, and remove those outside the window when checking a new event.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The edge case is when multiple events have the same timestamp, ensure you handle them in order and count them correctly within the window.

</details>
